title: Suikoden V
subtitle: A prince gathers a country around him

body: Suikoden V is a PlayStation 2 role-playing game developed by Konami and Hudson Soft, first released in Japan on 23 February 2006. The Prince of Falena becomes caught in the political struggles of his homeland, travelling to gather allies as the conflict develops. Set before the first Suikoden, it returns the series to a story where a large cast gives a national crisis a personal scale. Recruitment is part of the journey rather than an activity separated from it. Every new companion can make the prince's cause more than a claim inherited at court.

New recruits often have their own conditions or short quests, encouraging the player to investigate people and places beyond the next main objective. Towns provide information, equipment and opportunities to improve weapons or learn skills. More than sixty characters can take part in combat, while others support the group in different ways. The growing community therefore has uses beyond filling a roster. A return visit may reveal somebody who can now be persuaded to join, connecting the player's attention to the world with the strength of the alliance being built.

Takahiro Sakiyama directed the game, with Kazuyoshi Tsugawa writing its account of Falena's competing interests. The viewpoint and party structure recall aspects of the earlier Suikoden games while using three-dimensional environments and characters. Released internationally during 2006, it became the final main numbered entry in the original series. Its appeal rests on the connection between individual recruitment and larger events. The prince's travels are not only a route through the plot: they are the means by which a divided country gradually acquires a group capable of changing its direction.
